verdict.rationale: vLLM installs locally via pip/uv or from source (vllm-gh-1, vllm-gh-2, vllm-docs-18), so inference runs on your own hardware. The docs reference an offline-inference mode (vllm-docs-25), and supported hardware includes consumer-relevant targets such as x86/ARM CPUs, NVIDIA/AMD GPUs and Apple Silicon (vllm-docs-11). Quantization lets large models fit on a wider range of devices (vllm-docs-22), and the OpenAI-compatible server can be self-hosted (vllm-docs-27, vllm-docs-26). missing for 10: an explicit first-party statement that prompts and data never leave the device (e.g., no telemetry or fully air-gapped operation), and independent hands-on corroboration of purely local, private use on a single personal machine.
